_readme: Authoritative Local generation catalog. Templates own their reasoning prompt and typed slots. Assessment points define what may be tested and the difficulty range after variables are bound.

evidence_types.name: Module Graph
evidence_types.description: Source modules and their high-level organisation.

evidence_types.name: Data Flow
evidence_types.description: Functions and paths that move or transform data.

evidence_types.name: Control Flow
evidence_types.description: Functions and paths containing branches, loops, and state changes.

evidence_types.name: Symbol Table
evidence_types.description: Declared classes, functions, methods, and module-level symbols.

evidence_types.name: Complexity Analysis
evidence_types.description: Heuristic function-size, loop, branch, and call indicators.

evidence_types.name: Test Discovery
evidence_types.description: Discovered test files and test-like functions.

evidence_types.name: API Discovery
evidence_types.description: Routes, endpoints, requests, responses, and external communication.

evidence_types.name: SQL Analysis
evidence_types.description: SQL files, statements, schemas, and persistence operations.

assessment_points.name: Package Purpose
assessment_points.description: Why an imported Python package is present and what it contributes to this project.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify the general purpose of a common package.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain a package's evidenced, project-specific use.

assessment_points.query: python package library import dependency purpose project use

assessment_points.name: Module / Component Responsibility
assessment_points.description: The responsibility, boundary, and downstream contribution of a module or component.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a named module or component.
difficulty_anchors.3: Relate its responsibility to another component or downstream effect.

assessment_points.query: module component responsibility boundary role downstream

assessment_points.name: Function Input / Output Contract
assessment_points.description: A function's accepted inputs, returned structure, side effects, and caller expectations.

difficulty_anchors.1: Read an explicit parameter or return form.
difficulty_anchors.2: Infer the concrete input or output structure from the function body.
difficulty_anchors.3: Explain the contract's effect on a caller or downstream stage.

assessment_points.query: function parameter input return output type format side effect caller

assessment_points.name: Data Source / Acquisition
assessment_points.description: Where data originates and how Python retrieves, loads, or scrapes it.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify the source, file, API, or acquisition library.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain request parameters and the retrieved format.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace pagination, batching, quota, or repeated acquisition behavior.

assessment_points.query: data source acquire retrieve load scrape api request file pagination batch quota

assessment_points.name: External Interface Contract
assessment_points.description: API endpoints, MQTT topics, request/response payloads, and producer-consumer expectations.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify an endpoint, topic, method, or payload field.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace the contract between producer and consumer.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse the consequence of a contract or payload change.

assessment_points.query: api endpoint mqtt topic request response payload producer consumer contract

assessment_points.name: Data Format / Structure
assessment_points.description: The fields, types, shapes, and conversions of CSV, JSON, DataFrame, and record structures.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a data format, field, or basic structure.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain a format or type conversion.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace how a structural mismatch affects a downstream operation.

assessment_points.query: csv json dataframe record field column type format schema conversion

assessment_points.name: Cleaning / Missing Values
assessment_points.description: Deduplication, filtering, null handling, type correction, and consistency rules.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a cleaning operation used by the project.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain the rule applied to invalid, duplicate, or missing data.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict the cleaned result for a concrete input.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse a faulty cleaning policy or an unhandled anomaly.

assessment_points.query: clean filter missing null deduplicate duplicate type convert inconsistent invalid

assessment_points.name: Transformation / Aggregation
assessment_points.description: How records are mapped, grouped, aggregated, reshaped, or reduced to a new grain.

difficulty_anchors.2: Explain the direct purpose of a transformation.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict the transformed values, shape, or aggregation grain.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose an incorrect transformation or aggregation result.

assessment_points.query: transform map group aggregate reshape grain calculate dataframe

assessment_points.name: Integration / Entity Matching
assessment_points.description: How datasets are joined and how records, facilities, units, or identifiers are matched.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify the join or matching key.
difficulty_anchors.3: Explain how two project datasets are integrated.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse unmatched, duplicated, or wrong-grain integration results.

assessment_points.query: integrate join merge match identifier facility unit key grain

assessment_points.name: Data Augmentation / Enrichment
assessment_points.description: How external attributes such as geolocation are acquired, matched, and added to existing records.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify the enrichment source and added attribute.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace how enrichment data is matched and attached.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse incomplete matches, API failures, or enrichment quality.

assessment_points.query: augment enrich geocode location coordinates external attribute match

assessment_points.name: Pipeline / Data Flow
assessment_points.description: The order and direction of data movement across acquisition, processing, storage, publishing, and presentation.

difficulty_anchors.3: Trace a multi-stage workflow and intermediate forms.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse a cross-component consequence or broken pipeline path.

assessment_points.query: pipeline workflow data flow source destination stage order intermediate

assessment_points.name: Persistence / Schema Integrity
assessment_points.description: Tables, keys, relationships, constraints, persistence operations, and stored data grain.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a table, column, or persistence technology.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain a table's purpose or a basic key constraint.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace how records are written and related at the intended grain.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse a schema, constraint, or integrity failure.

assessment_points.query: database table column primary key foreign key constraint persist sql grain integrity

assessment_points.name: Caching / Materialisation
assessment_points.description: Why intermediate data is persisted and how caching limits repeated retrieval or processing.

difficulty_anchors.2: Explain why a cached file or materialised dataset exists.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace when cached versus fresh data is used.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse stale data, invalidation, or unnecessary repeated work.

assessment_points.query: cache materialize csv persist reuse refresh stale invalidation api calls

assessment_points.name: Streaming / Event Behaviour
assessment_points.description: Publishing, subscribing, event-time order, message delay, delta detection, and continuous execution.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify publisher, subscriber, topic, or message direction.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace ordered or delta-only streaming behaviour.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse duplicate, stale, out-of-order, or continuously repeated events.

assessment_points.query: mqtt publish subscribe stream event order delay delta continuous message

assessment_points.name: Condition / State Behaviour
assessment_points.description: Observable branch outcomes, state changes, loop behaviour, and shared runtime state.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify the direct outcome of a visible condition.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict multiple assignments, calls, or state changes along a path.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse state-dependent behaviour across functions or iterations.

assessment_points.query: condition branch loop state assignment return side effect outcome

assessment_points.name: Failure Handling / Recovery
assessment_points.description: Exceptions, retries, timeout handling, fallback paths, cleanup, and recovery behaviour.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify an exception, guard, retry, or cleanup action.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict the behaviour of an evidenced failure path.
difficulty_anchors.4: Diagnose an incomplete or harmful recovery path.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate a recovery design across API, storage, or streaming boundaries.

assessment_points.query: error exception timeout retry fallback cleanup recovery failure

assessment_points.name: Configuration / Security / Validation
assessment_points.description: Environment configuration, secrets, input validation, authentication, authorization, and safe handling.

difficulty_anchors.1: Identify a configuration source or protected value.
difficulty_anchors.2: Explain how configuration or validation is used by one component.
difficulty_anchors.3: Trace a validated or rejected input through the project.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse the consequence of missing validation, exposed secrets, or incorrect authorization.

assessment_points.query: environment config secret token validate authenticate authorize sanitize input

assessment_points.name: Testing / Data Quality Verification
assessment_points.description: Tests, assertions, quality checks, expected behaviour, and uncovered edge cases.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify what a test or quality check verifies.
difficulty_anchors.3: Predict whether a concrete input satisfies the verified behaviour.
difficulty_anchors.4: Analyse missing coverage or select a test that exposes a fault.

assessment_points.query: test assertion fixture expected quality check edge case coverage

assessment_points.name: Performance / Scalability
assessment_points.description: Repeated work, algorithmic cost, resource use, throughput, and project bottlenecks.

difficulty_anchors.2: Identify repeated work, a loop, or a resource-heavy operation.
difficulty_anchors.3: Explain the direct performance effect at the project's expected scale.
difficulty_anchors.4: Locate and reason about a measured or evidenced bottleneck.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate an optimisation and its correctness or resource trade-off.

assessment_points.query: performance complexity scale memory throughput repeated work bottleneck optimize

assessment_points.name: Design Decision / Change Impact
assessment_points.description: Why a design is used, what trade-offs it carries, and how a requirement change affects the system.

difficulty_anchors.3: Explain the project-specific rationale for a local design choice.
difficulty_anchors.4: Compare alternatives or trace the impact of a cross-component change.
difficulty_anchors.5: Evaluate a system-level trade-off and propose an evidence-consistent design.

assessment_points.query: design decision rationale tradeoff alternative requirement change impact architecture

templates.name: Contextual Use
templates.reasoning_prompt: Explain a project-specific use, relationship, or constraint supported by the supplied evidence.
stem_frames: In {context}, which statement correctly describes what {subject} does in this project?
In {context}, which statement correctly describes how the project uses {subject}?
templates.option_task: Test the subject's evidenced interaction, input/output, side effect, or downstream contribution. Do not test generic library knowledge or repeat what its name suggests.
templates.query: project-specific use interaction input output side effect dependency

required.label: concrete usage
required.query: import call use publish subscribe request transform save table

templates.name: Interaction / Flow
templates.reasoning_prompt: Trace an evidenced interaction, data path, or code path.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes how {subject} and {counterpart} work together?
Which statement correctly describes the link from {subject} to {counterpart}?
Which statement correctly describes what moves from {subject} to {counterpart}?
templates.option_task: Test an evidenced direction, ordering, transferred data, or cross-component consequence. Every option must be a complete relational claim.
templates.query: workflow order interaction source destination call flow dependency

required.label: evidenced relationship
required.query: source destination call order data flow dependency

templates.name: Condition / Outcome
templates.reasoning_prompt: Determine an observable outcome from the shown condition and code.
stem_frames: In the code below, what happens when {condition}?
templates.option_task: State exact calls, assignments, output, exceptions, or return behavior visible in the complete shown branch.
templates.query: condition branch state outcome exception return side effect

required.label: conditional code
required.query: if else try except match return set update

templates.name: Code Explain
templates.reasoning_prompt: Explain the complete evidenced effect of the shown code.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes what the code below does?
templates.option_task: Test the complete visible effect, including material calls, transformations, state changes, and return behavior.
templates.query: implementation effect transformation state return code

templates.name: Fault / Correction
templates.reasoning_prompt: Reason about one explicit hypothetical change and the behavior it would break.
stem_frames: A developer changes the code to {mutation}. Which statement correctly describes the problem this causes and how to fix it?
templates.option_task: Exactly one option must pair the observable consequence of the explicit hypothetical mutation with the correction that restores the shown behavior. Do not claim the original code is faulty.
templates.query: hypothetical change consequence correction condition return call

templates.name: Requirement / Change
templates.reasoning_prompt: Choose a change that meets a concrete requirement while preserving shown behavior.
stem_frames: The code must {requirement}. Which option should be added at INSERT HERE without changing the current behavior?
templates.option_task: Each option must be a short syntactically plausible snippet for the marked location. Exactly one must satisfy the stated requirement and preserve the visible control/data flow.
templates.query: requirement insert extend log validate preserve behavior

templates.name: Constraint / Verification
templates.reasoning_prompt: Explain a concrete, evidenced constraint or verified behaviour.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes the rule for {subject}?
Which statement correctly describes the checked behavior of {subject}?
templates.option_task: Test a concrete schema rule, validation guard, test expectation, security condition, data-quality rule, or measured complexity indicator. Do not ask for an undocumented design preference.
templates.query: constraint validation assertion schema integrity guard complexity

required.label: verifiable constraint
required.query: constraint not null primary key assertion validate guard loop branch

templates.name: Approach Used
templates.reasoning_prompt: Identify the project approach shown by the supplied evidence.
stem_frames: In {context}, which statement correctly describes the approach used for {subject}?
templates.option_task: Describe the actual project approach, such as batch loading, repeated polling, caching, streaming, or background processing. Do not test only a general definition.
templates.query: approach method batch polling cache streaming background process

required.label: project approach
required.query: load fetch poll cache publish subscribe save process

templates.name: Data Flow Selection
templates.reasoning_prompt: Choose the project data flow that matches the supplied evidence.
stem_frames: Which flow correctly shows how data moves from {source} to {destination}?
templates.option_task: Each option must be a complete ordered flow. Use clear arrows and include only stages supported by the evidence.
templates.query: data flow source stage destination order pipeline

required.label: ordered data flow
required.query: source destination stage order data moves

templates.name: Source and Method
templates.reasoning_prompt: Match a project data source or service with the way the project uses it.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly matches {subject} with the way it gets or sends data?
templates.option_task: Match the named source, service, or component with its real method, such as an API request, file load, database query, publish, or subscribe action.
templates.query: source method api request file load query publish subscribe

required.label: source and method
required.query: request read load query publish subscribe

templates.name: Stage Responsibility
templates.reasoning_prompt: Identify the job of a project stage or component from the supplied evidence.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes the job of {subject} in the data process?
templates.option_task: Describe what the stage receives, does, and passes on. Keep each option focused on one clear project responsibility.
templates.query: stage component responsibility input process output pipeline

templates.name: Processing Mode
templates.reasoning_prompt: Identify how the project processes data over time.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes how {subject} processes data?
templates.option_task: Describe the evidenced mode in simple terms, such as one-time batch work, repeated polling, cached replay, continuous messages, or background updates.
templates.query: batch repeated polling continuous stream replay background loop delay

required.label: processing mode
required.query: loop repeat delay batch stream publish subscribe

templates.name: Data Grain
templates.reasoning_prompt: Identify what one project record or message represents.
stem_frames: Which statement correctly describes what one record in {subject} represents?
templates.option_task: State the unit represented by one row, record, or message, including keys such as facility, unit, region, or time when the evidence supports them.
templates.query: record row message grain facility unit region timestamp key

required.label: record structure
required.query: record row field key facility unit region time

topics.name: Architecture
topics.description: Internal components, boundaries, dependencies, and how project parts work together.
topics.query: architecture module package dependency layer component boundary structure

topics.name: Integration / API
topics.description: External APIs, services, message queues, contracts, payloads, failures, and retries.
topics.query: integration api endpoint request response client payload mqtt publish subscribe external service retry

topics.name: Workflow / Data Flow
topics.description: How control or data moves from inputs through processing stages to outputs.
topics.query: workflow data flow pipeline input output transform validate load save process stage

topics.name: Implementation / Code Logic
topics.description: Local rules, transformations, conditions, state changes, and implementation behavior.
topics.query: implementation code logic function condition state behavior transformation calculation

topics.name: Data Modelling
topics.description: Persistence, schemas, relationships, queries, constraints, and data integrity.
topics.query: database schema table query sql transaction persist model record relationship constraint

topics.name: Security
topics.description: Validation, authentication, authorization, secrets, and safe data handling.
topics.query: security authenticate authorize permission input validation secret token encrypt sanitize

topics.name: Testing
topics.description: Test cases, assertions, expected behavior, boundaries, and fault detection.
topics.query: test testing assertion fixture validate expected error boundary behavior

topics.name: Complexity
topics.description: Time, space, scalability, resource use, and performance implications.
topics.query: complexity performance efficient optimize scalability time space memory loop

topics.name: OOP
topics.description: Classes, objects, encapsulation, inheritance, composition, and collaboration.
topics.query: oop object class method inheritance composition interface encapsulation polymorphism
